note: Shows frontier reasoning models collapse completely past a complexity threshold, the strongest evidence yet against vendor reasoning claims.
title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity

reading.body:
Frontier reasoning models collapse completely past a specific complexity threshold, which this paper presents as the strongest evidence yet against vendor claims of general reasoning ability.

Complete collapse, rather than gradual degradation, is the important detail. A model that gets gradually worse as problems get harder is behaving the way a system with limited but real reasoning would behave. A model that performs well below a threshold and then fails entirely above it is behaving more like a system that was pattern-matching to problem shapes it had effectively memorized, rather than reasoning through structure it had never seen.

The paper does not identify which specific architectural change would raise that threshold, only that the threshold exists and where it falls for the models tested.

explain_beginner: New AI models claim to show their thinking before answering questions. This study tested whether they actually think better than older models. Using puzzle games with different difficulty levels, researchers found these reasoning models perform well on medium-difficulty tasks but completely fail on harder problems. Surprisingly, they stop trying harder even when they could, suggesting their claimed thinking process has real limits that companies haven't fully disclosed.
explain_business: Organizations considering investments in advanced reasoning models should recognize they perform reliably only on medium-difficulty problems. Beyond that threshold, performance degrades completely, regardless of additional computational resources. This directly impacts use cases requiring complex analysis or high-stakes decision support. Decision-makers should evaluate actual performance ceilings for their specific problem domains rather than relying on vendor benchmarks, as claimed reasoning improvements may not translate to real-world applications.
explain_practitioner: We evaluated Large Reasoning Models using controlled puzzle environments enabling precise complexity manipulation. Analysis included final accuracy and reasoning traces across three regimes: low-complexity favors standard LLMs, medium-complexity favors LRMs, and high-complexity causes total collapse in both. LRMs exhibit token budget decline despite available capacity and struggle with exact computation and algorithmic reasoning. This reveals fundamental limitations in current reasoning architectures beyond benchmark contamination issues.
